slidetranscripts.slidetranscript:
<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Choose Your Own PBIS Coaching Adventure! 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Within this adventure, you will be playing the role of a coach at a school implementing PBIS. Each choice you make will lead to relevant outcomes, so choose wisely!
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Your school is working to install Tier 1 PBIS as a part of an MTSS framework. The School Leadership Team (or SLT) is meeting, but the administrator is not coming to meetings or staying for the full meeting time. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Select next to continue.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="Single" SpacingBefore="6" /> <Span Text="What is the coaching opportunity here?" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The School Leadership Team continues to meet without your administrator. During the next three meetings, the School Leadership Team makes plans to utilize the upcoming staff professional development to gather staff input on various components and products for the School-wide PBIS kick-off. Following each of the meetings, the team meeting notes are emailed to the administrator. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Less than a week before the staff professional development is to be held, the administrator reaches out to you (the coach) and lets you know that the district changed the professional development schedule weeks ago to address some new priorities. As a result, there will not be time for the School-wide PBIS work at the upcoming staff meeting. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="You and the rest of the school leadership team are understandably frustrated. A lot of time and effort has gone into preparing for the upcoming staff professional development. The team members are feeling unsupported by the administrator and wondering if their work is valued. One team member openly states that if the administrator had been a part of these meetings all along like he was supposed to be, the team would have known about the district's change of plans for professional development. With this information, they could have spent their time in a different way to ensure the critical School-wide PBIS work continued to move forward. As the coach, you are second guessing your decision to focus on strengthening the communication with the administrator after meetings in an attempt to compensate for the fact that he was not attending. Select next to continue." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="In this case, there was a missed opportunity to identify the correct coaching concept and to apply coaching foundation skills to address the situation.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="As a coach, what do you think you should do next?" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The coaching opportunity was related to the functioning of the School Leadership Team, in particular the importance of the active involvement of the school's administrator." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="You set up a meeting with the District's Coach Coordinator. You raise the concern that your school's administrator is not attending the school leadership team meetings, explaining that during the last two meetings the administrator either came late or left very early, and the meeting prior to that he did not come at all. You are concerned that if the administrator does not come to meetings, the team cannot accomplish the work needed to be done to install School-wide PBIS You mention that the rest of the team is on board and working hard towards the kick-off of PBIS in the fall, but that this work may fall to the wayside if the administrator does not do his part. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The District Coach Coordinator takes your concern to the district implementation team as a barrier, basically calling out your school's administrator for not fully participating in the school leadership team meetings and as a result not truly leading the MTSS implementation in the building
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Later that week, your school's administrator calls you to his office to discuss the sequence of events that led to the concern being raised to the district implementation team. He is very unhappy that you did not come directly to him with your concern. As a result, the trust between you, as the coach, and the administrator has been damaged. The administrator is wary of being called out by the district implementation team in the future. While he is coming to all of the school leadership team meetings, his approach is that of compliance with the process rather than truly leading the installation and implementation of School-wide P.B.I.S. The rest of the team notices the tension between you and the administrator. They wonder if PBIS will get off the ground, and if it does if it will be sustained without the support from the principal. Select next to continue." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="By taking this approach, you jumped to a solution that did not take into account maintaining the relationship with your school's administrator. A better choice would have been to focus on the school leadership team functioning. See how that plays out. " /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="You decide to set up a meeting with your school's administrator to discuss the importance of her participation on the School Leadership Team.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="What is the best step to take while preparing for the meeting?" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Well done! You recognized the coaching opportunity related to the functioning of the School Leadership Team, in particular the importance of the active involvement of the school's administrator. You successfully applied your coaching foundation skills and came up with a solution with the administrator." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="Single" SpacingBefore="6" /> <Span Text="The administrator is now attending your School Leadership Team meetings routinely and is taking an active role. However, a potential new issue has arisen in regards to team functioning Over the course of the last 3 School Leadership Team meetings, you have noticed that only 2 of the 6 team members are actively participating in the meeting and contributing to the action steps. While you know active participation from all members is important to team functioning, you debate whether or not this needs to be addressed. The team is still able to get the installation checklist items done between team training events and it looks like your school is on track for a strong kick-off of School-wide PBIS in the fall. Identify the coaching opportunity and your next step." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Having only a couple of team members actively involved in the meetings and the action items can lead to burnout of team members quickly. In addition, a situation like this runs the risk of having limited buy-in across the team as well. While it is great that progress is being made on the installation checklist items, there is still a coaching opportunity here. " /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="Single" SpacingBefore="6" /> <Span Text="During the next meeting with your administrator, you start off the conversation by acknowledging the leadership that the administrator has already demonstrated related to the readiness work for School-wide P.B.I.S. in the building, highlighting the ways that his presence and leadership has helped with initial exploration and readiness work. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="Single" SpacingBefore="6" /> <Span Text="You then bring the conversation around to the current situation. While the administrator plays a crucial role in the functioning of the school leadership team, currently he is unable to be present for all or part of the School Leadership Team meetings. You ask what is preventing him from being able to attend, and you offer to work together to support his attendance and participation on the team. It turns out that meeting right after school on Wednesdays is difficult for him because there are often other district meetings later in the afternoon and evening that same day that are pulling his attention and availability away from the School Leadership Team. The administrator is resistant to the idea of changing the meeting date or time to accommodate his schedule. He begins to push for a strong communication plan to keep him in the loop; he does not want the rest of the team to be frustrated because they have to reschedule to accommodate his individual needs. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="Single" SpacingBefore="6" /> <Span Text="As the coach, you provide the upside of making the change to accommodate the administrator's conflicts. You address current frustrations developing in the team members because he is not present, and you indicate that progress will pick up because the team will not have to find time to run things by him outside of the meeting. You also let him know the downside you foresee if you do not change the meeting day or time, including continued and increased frustration from the team when the work has to slow down or stop during the meeting because he is not present to make decisions, and the inability to benefit from his perspective and expertise as the instructional leader of the school, since the team lacks the larger district perspective that he brings to the table. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="Single" SpacingBefore="6" /> <Span Text="As a result of this meeting, the administrator agrees that the first agenda item for the next meeting is to reschedule the monthly school leadership team meetings to ensure his full participation. Together, you craft the rationale for the change. Select next to continue." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="Single" SpacingBefore="6" /> <Span Text="Given the low participation, you prompt the team to communicate school-wide a need to have more staff involved in the work of this team. The team decides to recruit more staff that are willing to take on some of the installation activities. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="Single" SpacingBefore="6" /> <Span Text="While the 2 team members who have been most actively involved reluctantly agree with this plan, in private they share their frustration. They feel that the other team members are supposed to be a part of leading this work but are just showing up. They also express concerns about the perception that may come with recruiting more help when team members are not actively involved. They are wondering why these other people are on the team in the first place. Tensions begin to develop between team members." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Your instinct to have more than the two active team members involved is spot on. However, this solution has created some additional adaptive challenge. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="As a coach, what do you think you should do next?" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="As the coach, you could have used your getting and giving information coaching foundation skill as well as the using rationales to make connections. You could have also have tapped into the maintaining relationships by first discussing this concern with the principal and co-developing a plan to support improvement in the team functioning." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="0" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20" SpacingBefore="0" SpacingAfter="0"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="You determine that lack of active participation by all team members is a barrier and decide to record this on the barrier log for the District Implementation Team to address. In the meantime, you rest assured that the team is on track because the installation checklist items are getting done. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="0" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20" SpacingBefore="0" SpacingAfter="0"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="0" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20" SpacingBefore="0" SpacingAfter="0"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Over the next couple of School Leadership Team meetings, your focus as team coach has shifted from improving team functioning to compliance in the form of getting tasks on the installation checklist completed alongside the two participating team members. Though you feel good that the work is moving forward, you become increasingly concerned as you observe that the rest of the team seems less and less invested in the work of installing School-wide PBIS. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="0" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20" SpacingBefore="0" SpacingAfter="0"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="0" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20" SpacingBefore="0" SpacingAfter="0"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="At the next District Implementation Team meeting, the barrier you identified is turned back to your building's administrator. The administrator comes back to the idea that as long as the installation checklist items are getting completed, things must be okay. Over time, the two members carrying the load of the work begin to complain that being a part of the team is too time consuming. You worry they may ask to be taken off the team if things do not change regarding the whole team contributing to the work. A better choice would have been to focus on the school leadership team functioning. See how that plays out." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="What is the best way to focus on SLT functioning?" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="While your concern is legitimate, this approach may result in team members becoming defensive and/or cause team members to consider quitting the team. Your administrator could get upset by this approach and prefer that you raised the concern privately to co-develop a plan to address the concern. Please review your coaching foundational skills and make another selection." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Approaching the administrator with your concern is the right approach, however, when addressing an adaptive concern such as this, it is best to meet face to face for the conversation. Leveraging your observation skills to describe the concern fully and providing the administrator the opportunity to also share leverages your coaching skills of getting and giving information. " /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="You recognize the importance of having all School Leadership Team members actively involved and contributing to the team's action steps so that members who are participating do not become frustrated and also to ensure that the work is sustainable over time. You decide to schedule a meeting with the principal to share your observations and to ask for his help and support in addressing the concern.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Prior to your meeting, you develop a rationale with talking points that focus on the importance of all team members taking an active role. You also point out the risk over time to the team relationships and to the implementation of School-wide PBIS if only two members are doing all the work.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="During your meeting, you first share your observations on the completion of the installation checklist and celebrate the progress the team has made. You next raise the issue of team functioning, first asking your principal how he thinks the School Leadership Team is operating. Throughout the discussion, you share your observations of the unequal workload across team members. The principal supports your observations and the two of you develop a plan to lift your concerns to each team member individually.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The principal plans to meet with all the team members individually prior to the next School Leadership Team meeting. During those meetings, he will ask each team member how they feel the team is functioning and if they are still interested in the work. The two of you also decide to add to the next team meeting agenda a review of the roles and responsibilities of the School Leadership Team and to review the norms for the team. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="By recording your observations, developing a clear rationale for the importance of shared work, and including your principal in the process, you were able to address this barrier. Your attention to team functioning was a correct application of your coaching. Select next to continue." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Nicely done coach! You tapped into the getting and giving information coaching foundation skill as well as the using rationales to make connections. You also have tapped into the maintaining relationships by first discussing this concern with the principal and co-developing a plan to support improvement in the team functioning." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Following your last full staff meeting focused on developing an acknowledgment system as part of Tier 1 PBIS installation, a heated conversation arose. A few staff members came up to you, the School Leadership Team coach, stating that providing acknowledgments to students is like bribing them to behave, and at this age, students should just know the right things to do in school without being rewarded. " /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Identify the coaching opportunity and your next step." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Feeling a little overwhelmed trying to come up with a plan to convince staff to buy into the acknowledgement system all on your own, you wonder if any of the other coaches are dealing with this same issue. You decide to share your concern with the District Coach Coordinator by adding this as an item for the next Coaches Meeting. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The District Coach coordinator sees your request and adds it to the next month's agenda. Even though you have a School Leadership Team meeting coming up next week, you decide to leave this item off your team's agenda until you have had the opportunity to discuss it at your monthly coaches meeting.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="After 4 weeks have passed, you finally have your monthly Coaches Meeting. To get more context on your situation, the question is raised by the District Coach Coordinator, "Is this a technical or adaptive challenge your team is facing?" You share that you have not brought this to the team yet, so you are unsure if it will be technical or adaptive. The District Coach Coordinator is concerned. She notes that you are correct that the Monthly Coaches Meeting is an appropriate place to access professional learning on a topic. However, 4 weeks have now passed since you became aware of this potential barrier and it has not been communicated to the School Leadership Team, even though you had a team meeting. She is concerned the School Leadership Team may feel surprised when they find out. As a coach, you run the risk of trying to solve this challenge on your own if you do not bring it to the School Leadership Team first. She reminds you that addressing barriers like these requires the efforts of the whole team. She prompts you to ensure this barrier is on the agenda for the next team meeting. By the end of that meeting, clear next steps need to be identified to move the problem closer to a resolution. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Reflect on the feedback provided by the DC and try again." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="What is the best way to focus on staff buy-in for Schoolwide PBIS?" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="There are staff who are vocally opposed to one of the big ideas of school wide PBIS, which indicates there is work to be done. " /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Recall your role is a systems coach. This response is more instructional coaching which is outside of your role. Consider your coaching foundational skills and make another selection. " /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="By addressing this with only the administrator, you are missing out on the opportunity to use your getting and giving information coaching skills to better understand the lack of buy-in for acknowledgements. The rest of the SLT have valuable information about what they've seen and observed that could provide a more robust plan for addressing the lack of buy-in. " /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="This is clearly a barrier to implementing School-wide PBIS and one you should not try to tackle all on your own! It is a smart decision to bring this back to the School Leadership Team. Addressing staff resistance might turn into an adaptive challenge, and it will be important the team be prepared to come up with a plan. You decide to add "Staff Resistance to Acknowledgement System" to the School Leadership Team agenda. To support the team, you prepare to facilitate a discussion of strategies the School Leadership Team can take to address staff buy-in. Your goal is to have the team produce specific action steps to ensure that all staff understand the rationale for using the acknowledgement system, clearly communicate administration’s support of this approach, and provide the tools and resources they need to implement with fidelity. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="During the next School Leadership Team meeting, the team holds a discussion about getting all staff on board with the acknowledgement system. As the coach, you lead the team in a review of what has been done so far to gain staff buy-in. The team identifies that only the brief overview of the acknowledgement had been provided, without providing intentional opportunities for staff to discuss it and share their thoughts and concerns. The team makes a plan to recruit staff input by sending out a survey to ask (1) what concerns they have with implementing an acknowledgement system and (2) what additional support or learning they need to understand and successfully this essential component of School-wide PBIS. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Prior to the next team meeting, you review the responses and put together a brief summary to share with the School Leadership Team. Most staff report full buy-in for the acknowledgement system, requesting only additional learning on how it will be rolled out schoolwide. However, several staff indicate they want to understand the difference between acknowledging and bribing students. A few staff comment they want to know what this looks like at other schools. Using this data, the School Leadership Team develops a plan. First, they decide they will share an article with staff that differentiates acknowledgement from bribery that will be discussed at the next all staff meeting. Second, the team will recruit staff, including the school's principal, to share their positive experiences implementing an acknowledgement system. Finally, the principal will intentionally model the use of the acknowledgement system to recognize staff behavior, demonstrating a school wide integration of the practice. " /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Well done! You recognized the coaching opportunity related to the functioning of the School Leadership Team, in particular the importance of identifying barriers, adding them to the SLT agenda, and preparing to lead a discussion focused on creating action steps to remove the barrier. You successfully applied your coaching foundation skills and came up with a solution with the SLT. Your coaching adventure continues!" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="Single" SpacingBefore="6" /> <Span Text="Now that you have completed your PBIS Coaching adventure, it's time for your next adventure: real-life coaching!
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="Single" SpacingBefore="6" /> <Span Text="Remember: Each choice you make will lead to relevant outcomes, so choose wisely!" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>
